title: Hacer caso omiso de: ignorar deliberadamente algo

sections.content: Hacer caso omiso de (to disregard, to deliberately ignore) describes willfully paying no attention to something -- a ruling, a warning, a rule -- stronger than simply ignorar, since it implies the thing was clearly known and consciously set aside. It's followed by a noun phrase. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El Estado brasileño ha hecho, en gran medida, caso omiso de esta sentencia internacional.
items.english: The Brazilian state has, to a large extent, disregarded this international ruling.

items.spanish: Algunos gobiernos hicieron caso omiso de las recomendaciones de organismos internacionales de derechos humanos.
items.english: Some governments disregarded the recommendations of international human rights bodies.

items.spanish: Hacer caso omiso de un fallo judicial firme resulta, en principio, incompatible con el propio Estado de derecho.
items.english: Disregarding a final judicial ruling is, in principle, incompatible with the rule of law itself.

items.spanish: El tribunal advirtió que no podía hacerse caso omiso de las obligaciones internacionales asumidas voluntariamente por el país.
items.english: The court warned that the international obligations voluntarily assumed by the country could not be disregarded.

sections.content: Hacer caso omiso de always implies the thing being ignored was known and deliberately set aside -- for simply not noticing something, use no darse cuenta de instead, which carries no implication of intent.
